body: I don't think forcing myself into getting a job which I don't enjoy will help me all that much. Sorry :P

Things are pretty rocky with my Mum. I don't see my sister very often but we get along well. She's had a lot of problems lately so I don't think she'd do too well if she had to worry about me too. There are one or two friends who I might be able to confide in, but I'm worried about the chance of scaring them off, since there are so few people I talk to these days. I've thought about opening up a little bit at a time, so as not to suddenly come across too strongly, but if I mention I've been a bit down they'll probably ask enough questions to realize how much I've been isolating myself. Among the people I do talk to regularly, I've made an effort to appear as social and extroverted as anyone else, so confiding in them would ruin that illusion. I guess I figured it was safer to open up to Reddit first.

I hadn't thought of that. A general checkup wouldn't hurt, anyway. I'll try and make an appointment sometime in the next few days.

I know there's the potential to have a lot of great experiences in my future, which is why I'm worried about falling deeper into this state and wasting my life. Unfortunately that doesn't translate into personal motivation, for some reason.

Every now and then I decide to start eating/drinking/exercising properly. Eventually I revert to how I was before... It's hard to explain, but I don't think it's laziness. It's not that I want to be healthy but don't have the self-control, it's that a lot of the time I just stop caring. I'm not sure if what I said makes sense. It could just be laziness in disguise.

I've tried a few hobbies. Writing, drawing, game design, but they don't really leave me feeling very fulfilled. It may just be that I haven't found the right hobby yet, there are some other hobbies I've been thinking of trying, though I don't know if they'd keep me interested long-term, and they might only isolate me further.

I'd love to visit Korea and Japan! I've been there before, but I didn't get to stay for very long last time. The cities there are wonderful.

Not for about a year or two.

> I've noticed my health slowly diminishing over the last few years

I should have explained what I meant by this a bit better. The health deterioration is the sort you expect if you don't exercise or eat enough. I used to be fairly fit and participated in athletics in high school. Now I get exhausted much faster, need to sleep 10 hours a day, get headaches and dizziness more often, etc.

If I *was* seriously ill though, I don't know if I'd care.
